transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose it’s not anything too dramatic, but I’ve noticed I’m sort of… always on the go. Even on a quiet day at home, I’ll be up and moving from one thing to another — the garden club list, then my knitting bag, then some travel papers — and I haven’t really finished the first thing before I’m onto the next. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it’s been enough that I thought I should ask about it.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually energetic or needing less sleep lately?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I do keep busy, but I wouldn’t say I’ve suddenly felt unusually energetic or that I don’t need sleep. At least, not that I’ve noticed. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking?
Have you had any periods recently where you felt unusually high-spirited, irritable, or 'on top of the world' for several days in a row?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have good days, of course, and I can get a little snappy like anyone, but not several days where I felt on top of the world or anything like that. At least, I haven’t noticed that. Is that helpful?
Have you felt down, sad, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have quiet days or days where I’m not quite myself, but not most of the day nearly every day like that, and I haven’t lost interest in the things I usually like. At least, not in the way you’re describing, I don’t think.
Do you ever feel restless or find yourself unable to sit still for very long?

A little, yes. I wouldn’t say I’m bouncing off the walls or anything, but if I have to sit still too long, I get this sort of stirred-up feeling inside. Then I feel like I should stand up, straighten something, or go check on something. I don’t know if that counts as restlessness, but that’s what it feels like.
Has this restlessness or need to keep moving been something you've always had, or is it something that's gotten worse recently?

I think it’s probably always been there, just maybe not as noticeable now. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but even back in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but kind of scattered. They’d say I lost papers, talked out of turn sometimes, and wiggled in my seat before I finished my work. So… yes, I guess it goes back pretty far. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you find it hard to focus or stay on task, especially when something isn’t really interesting or requires a lot of sustained attention?

Yes, I suppose so, though I try not to let it get too obvious. Like, I can start out listening at a planning meeting, or reading the church bulletin, and I mean to pay attention. But after a little while I’ll realize I’ve missed half of what was said, or I’ve read the words but didn’t really take them in. It’s worse when it’s not especially interesting or it goes on for a while. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Do these difficulties with staying focused or feeling restless happen in different parts of your life, like at home, at church, or when you're out with friends, or are they mostly just happening in one place?

It’s not just one place, no. I wish I could say it was only at home, but it does show up in other places too. At home my husband will sometimes have to check behind me about plans or what we said we were going to do, and at the community center the other volunteers have gotten to where they sort of double-check me too.

I don’t mean I’m completely unreliable, but… it has caused some strain, honestly. They can’t always count on me to keep the plans straight unless someone helps me with it. Is that what you’re asking?

Have these difficulties with focus and restlessness caused you noticeable problems in more than one area of your life, like at home, at church, or with friends, such as missing important details, making careless mistakes, or having trouble organizing tasks?

Yes… I think it has, though I hate to say it that strongly. It’s caused some real strain at home, and at the community center too. My husband will check behind me about plans, and the other volunteers sort of do the same, because they can’t always count on me to keep everything straight on my own.

I don’t mean I’m not trying, because I am. But without someone double-checking, things can get mixed up. Is that what you’re asking?
